title: Ostomy Supply Program Written Orders and Authorization Grants
content:
Every Ostomy Supply Program shipment rests on a written order from the treating prescriber that names the item, the billing units per 30 days, the order date and the prescriber's NPI.

## Written orders

The order is valid for the tier's written order validity, in calendar months counted from its order date, the valid-through date being the day before the same calendar day that many months later (falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist); Larkfield records that valid-through date when the order is received.

*Hypothetical illustration:* with a 12-month validity, an order dated 15 March is valid through 14 March of the following year.

A written order on file is the condition for both a prior authorization request and an authorization grant.

## Authorization grants

| Tier type | How the authorization grant arises | Span of the grant |
|---|---|---|
| Tiers where prior authorization is required | Once the written order is on file, Larkfield submits a prior authorization request to the payer and moves the program from referral received to pending authorization. The payer's approval is recorded as an authorization grant on the payer prior authorization basis, carrying the payer's PA reference, the approved units and the approved span. | The tier's prior authorization validity in calendar months from the decision date, unless the payer's approval states an earlier valid-through date, in which case the payer's date governs. |
| Tiers where prior authorization is not required | Larkfield records the authorization grant itself on the basis of the written order (the written order basis, or the self-pay order basis on the self-pay tier), for the billing units the order covers within that span. | From the order date through the order's valid-through date. |

## Request speed

A prior authorization request is submitted as expedited only when the prescriber states on the order that waiting the standard decision time could seriously jeopardize the patient's life or health; otherwise it is standard. The payer is expected to decide within the tier's standard decision time in calendar days of a standard request, or the tier's expedited decision time in hours of an expedited one.

## Renewals

A renewal request for a prior authorization may be submitted no earlier than the tier's renewal lead in calendar days before the valid-through date of the authorization it renews, counted backward in calendar days from that valid-through date with the earliest submission day itself allowed, and it requires a written order that is valid beyond that valid-through date.

| Hypothetical case (renewal lead of 30 days, valid-through on day 100) | Submission permitted? |
|---|---|
| Submitted on day 69 | No - earlier than the earliest day |
| Submitted on day 70 | Yes - the earliest day itself is allowed |
| Submitted on day 85, written order valid through day 100 only | No - the order is not valid beyond the valid-through date |

## Activation, denials and clinical documents

- A program is activated only when an authorization grant on file for the program is valid on the activation date.
- A payer denial of a prior authorization is recorded with the payer's denial reason; the program stays in pending authorization while the prescriber supplies further documentation or a new request is made, and it closes only under the program's hold and closure rules.
- Clinical documents are recorded with the purpose they serve and the visit date they document, and a document serves only the purpose recorded on it.
